messages:
maria: Heads up — after last night's KMS key rotation some tenants report SAML logins failing. Pattern: they use audience wildcard in assertion (e.g. https://app.redwood.ai/*). Also SCIM provisioning for those tenants shows duplicate externalId errors.

raj: I see the same on authn-proxy logs. KMS decrypt errors intermittently: 
```ERROR authn-proxy: decrypt failed: kms:AccessDenied for projects/redwood/.../cryptoKeys/rotate-2026
request_id=abc123
``` 

katie: Could be two independent things. We rolled a proxy change 03/18 that tightened audience checks (no wildcard allowed). If assertion has wildcard it now fails audience validation rather than signing.

charu: correct — feature 'strict_audience_match' shipped in canary. It intentionally rejects wildcard audiences. We added it because of CVE-2025-XXXX where wildcard audiences allowed token confusion.

maria: OK, so why did SCIM duplicate extids show up? That's a separate symptom but same tenant set.

raj: SCIM flow: we encrypt user.externalId with KMS-managed context. After rotate we attempted to rewrap but some backends still using old key context; create returns 201 then subsequent reconcile sees different extid -> 409 duplicate.

katie: Repro: SAML Assertion snippet showing audience
```xml
<saml:Audience>https://app.redwood.ai/*</saml:Audience>
```
Proxy now compares full string equality; wildcard fails.

charu: Temp mitigation options:
- flip rollout flag off (strict_audience_match=false)
- re-run extid rewrap job to canonicalize to new KMS wrapping
- allow a fallback verification that uses hostname prefix match for legacy tenants

ops: deploying flag rollback for a small subset now (:spinner:)

security-bot: Alert created SEC-2026-189; affected_requests=137; severity=medium; linked ticket SYS-4872

maria: We need a runbook to resolve safely without reintroducing the CVE vector. Ideas?

raj: Runbook sketch:
1) Identify tenants using wildcard audience via logs/query: `select tenant_id from sso_audits where audience like '%*'`
2) For those tenants, run KMS rewrap backfill for scim.extid with idempotent job (safe-rewrap v2)
3) Temporarily allow legacy_audience_fallback for only those tenant IDs in authn-proxy config
4) Monitor 5xx/KMS errors and authn success rate
5) Re-enable strict_audience_match after rewrap completes

katie: Config snippet for temporary fallback:
```yaml
authn_proxy:
  strict_audience_match: true
  legacy_audience_fallback_tenants:
    - tenant-123
    - tenant-456
```

charu: For the extid duplicates I'll run safe-rewrap job that calls `kms.decrypt(old_cipher)` -> compute canonical extid -> `kms.encrypt(new_cipher)` using new key alias. Will keep op-log and per-tenant dry-run first.

maria: Who can own each action? I can own postmortem + communication to customer success. charu you own rewrap. katie you push config change + feature flag gating. raj monitor and validate metrics.

ops: Canary rollback applied to 10% of traffic. Watchers: @katie @raj

security-bot: Audit log entry created: ACL-change=true KMS-rotation=true ticket=SEC-2026-189

maria: Thanks all — let's sync in 30m if smoke tests still failing. Please paste any failing log lines here.

raj: posting quick grep for remaining KMS denies:
`grep "kms:AccessDenied" /var/log/authn-proxy/*.log | wc -l` -> 14

katie: smoke authn success rate up from 78% -> 98% in canary. I'll start rewrap dry-run tomorrow 03/19 0400UTC

charu: dry-run queued. will report results here.

maria: adding note — don't run global rollback. Need audit trace for every step.

security-bot: Remediation checklist attached to SEC-2026-189
